segments.title:
What the budget
means for you
segments.say: Zimbabwe's 2027 budget is out. Here's what it means for your pocket.

segments.title: Cellphone import duty
segments.source: Finance Minister, 2027 Budget Statement (via NewZimbabwe, Zimbabwe Independent)
segments.say: Customs duty on imported cellphones drops from 25 percent to zero. On a 200 dollar phone at the border, that's 50 dollars of duty gone, though VAT can still apply.

segments.title: More in your pocket
segments.say: Earn up to 150 US dollars a month and you pay no income tax, up from 100. The tax on US dollar transfers drops from 2 percent to 1.75. And the minister says there are no new taxes.

segments.title: Also cheaper

cards.text: Duty on wheelchairs, hearing aids, glasses

segments.say: Duty on electric vehicles falls to 10 percent. Duty is removed on wheelchairs, hearing aids and glasses, and VAT on freshwater fish goes too.

segments.title: The whole budget
segments.label: TOTAL SPENDING · 2027
segments.source: Finance Minister via ZBC News · Zimbabwe Independent
segments.say: Total spending: 358.3 billion ZiG, about 12.8 billion US dollars, against revenue of 349.5 billion.

segments.title: Where the money goes
segments.say: Where it goes: schools get the most, 47.7 billion. Then health, 35.5. Debt, 31.2. Agriculture, 27.6. Public service, 21.5. Higher education, 15. Transport, 10.8.

segments.title: Out of every ZiG 100
segments.say: Put simply: out of every 100 ZiG the government spends, about 13 go to schools, 10 to health, and 9 to paying debts.

segments.title: What to watch
lines: These are proposals: Parliament still has to pass the budget
segments.disclaimer: Not financial advice. Sources: Finance Minister via ZBC News, Zimbabwe Independent, NewZimbabwe.
segments.say: Remember, these are proposals until Parliament passes them. Treasury expects growth of 3.5 percent in 2027. Not financial advice. Follow for more.
